solutions.independent_solution: The dashed graph in fig-29 is horizontal at x=3 m for all displayed times. Since coordinate never changes, v=delta x/delta t=0. It represents a stationary body at x=3 m, not positive motion at 3 m/s, motion along the time axis, or a body at the origin.

From the common starting coordinate 3 m and the actual labeled line slopes, x2(3)=3+1.5*3=7.5 m and x4(3)=3-1*3=0 m; line 4's zero crossing corroborates t=3. Separation is |x2-x4|=|7.5-0|=7.5 m. Equivalently relative velocity is 1.5-(-1)=2.5 m/s, times 3 s. Merely reporting a coordinate is not the general distance procedure even though x4 happens to equal zero at this queried time.

The fig-28 coordinate-time line has constant positive slope. Using actual ticks, (5-3)/(20-0)=2/20=+0.1 m/s; independently (3-0)/(0-(-30))=3/30=+0.1 m/s. Magnitude is 0.1 m/s, direction is the positive x direction. The 3-m intercept is not displacement from time zero, and apparent screen angle is not velocity.
